alex_dev: quick check — we saw a couple of production hits where upstream returned a 5xx mid-chunk and the client just got a truncated stream. proposing we standardize a deterministic midstream fallback that either resumes or gracefully aborts. ideas?

maya_sre: critical: we must not accidentally double-apply side-effects for tool-calls. resume only when the call is idempotent or the client opted in. Also concerned about state kept for resumes. TTL and caps needed. :warning:

sam_arch: rough proposal: assign an ephemeral resume id at ingress and require the client to send `x-rw-resume-id` for resumable streams. on upstream 5xx mid-stream, edge snapshots a small KV of last N tokens + model cursor and returns a `x-rw-resume-token` trailer to the client. client can call `POST /v1/resume` with that token to continue. this avoids blind retries.

jordan_pm: from UX POV we need two behaviors: "best-effort resume" (try to continue producing text) and "abort-and-retry" (client restarts request). which one do we default to? customers will care about determinism.

alex_dev: agree. default to abort for anything that may have side-effects. default to resume for pure generation/chat. quick state machine sketch:

```
STATE: STREAMING
on upstream 5xx ->
  if request.is_idempotent && resume_id present -> RESUME_STORED (return token)
  else -> GRACEFUL_ABORT (return trailer incomplete=1 + error)
```

maya_sre: size/retention rules: resume snapshots capped at 64KB, TTL 30s by default. evict LRU. instrument OOM and eviction metrics. also require resume-token to be single-use.

sam_arch: also need compatible semantics for model switching: if upstream fails due to OOM we can fall back to a smaller variant and resume from token. but must attach a definitive marker in trace/logs. cost tradeoff spelled out in route config.

ops-bot: FYI deploy checklist item created: "edge: resumable-streaming feature flag" — https://go/rw/edge-resume-ff

jordan_pm: metrics we should capture: resume_token_issued, resume_success, resume_abort_count, resume_latency_percentiles, resume_eviction_count. tie to billing to ensure resumed tokens don't bypass quota charging.

alex_dev: need API surface consensus: recommend trailer header `x-rw-resume-token` emitted only when incomplete. propagate `x-rw-resume-at` with token to indicate position. clients can call: `POST /v1/resume { token, prefer_model }`. also add `x-rw-resume-ttl` as header on token issue.

maya_sre: tests: simulate non-idempotent operations + resumed tokens; ensure resume path returns 409 or forced abort. include chaos tests where KV store is slow to ensure we fail closed.

sam_arch: example request/response snippet for docs:

```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <key>
  x-rw-resume-id: 9f1b7c4a
Body: streaming chunks...

-- stream --
chunk...
chunk...
Trailer: x-rw-resume-token: eyJ... (present if upstream failed mid-stream)
```

alex_dev: implementation notes: runtime will snapshot only the minimal decode state (kvcache pointer + last token window) not full model weights. we must ensure storage is encrypted and TTL enforced. also update tracing so resume tokens map to trace-id.

jordan_pm: feature flag rollout plan: start internal only, 2-week soak on canary, then 25% customers with opt-in, then GA after metrics look stable.

maya_sre: one more: ensure quota and billing attach to original request owner for any resumed tokens — prevent gaming.

sam_arch: I'll open a PR with the proto changes and an RFC addendum (includes state machine + TTLs + config knobs). will ping @alex_dev and @maya_sre for review.

alex_dev: perfect. thanks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rolling out feature flag scaffold to canary clusters this afternoon.

alex_dev: leaving this thread open for a couple days for followups; if there are no blockers we'll move PR -> code review.
